    interface Schema<T> {
        parse(self: self, value: unknown): T;
    }
    
    interface ObjectSchema<T> extends Schema<T> {}
    
    type Infer<T> = T extends Schema<infer O> ? O : never;
    type InferUnion<T extends Schema<unknown>[]> = Infer<T[number]>;
    
    declare object: <T extends table>() => ObjectSchema<T>;
    declare union: <T extends Schema<unknown>[]>(options: T) => Schema<InferUnion<T>>;
    
    local success = object<{
        status: "success";
        data: string;
    }>()
    
    -- Heterogeneity is irrelevant: the homogeneous constructor takes the same path.
    local homo = union({ success, success }):parse({})
    local h = homo.status
    
    -- A hand-written number-keyed record is NOT implicitly number-indexable: the
    -- array path is a rule about table CONSTRUCTORS in array contexts, not a
    -- read-side leniency. A post-widening record type is indistinguishable from
    -- this one, so making the read lenient would globally silence the error.
    type Lit = { 1: typeof success; 2: typeof success };
    type ByNumber = Lit[number]; -- error
                        ~~~~~~

    -- Per-UNION exclusion: a numeric-keyed record constituent keeps the object
    -- path, so the record wins and its excess-entry checking survives.
    type Rec = { 1: number; 2: string };
    local u: number[] | Rec = { 1, "two" }
    local u2: number[] | Rec = { 1, "two", true } -- error
